new_scholarship.description: The FWF ASTRA Awards are a career funding programme launched in July 2024 for advanced postdocs in Austria who already have experience with independent research (R3 level). The FWF awards between EUR 500,000 and EUR 1 million per project over five years, plus an additional EUR 200,000 tenure package for female principal investigators who secure a permanent position within the first three years. Proposals are submitted through the elane portal during a published annual application window, which was closed on the verification date.

new_scholarship.description: The DAAD Research Grants in Germany fund a research project at a state or state-recognised university or non-university research institute in Germany, carried out with a German scientific supervisor. Doctoral candidates may be funded for 2 to 12 months and early postdocs for 2 to 6 months; the grant cannot be extended and cannot be split within the funding period. programme_detail_official.description: The DAAD research grant offers doctoral candidates and early postdocs the opportunity to realise a research project at a state or state-recognised university or a non-university research institute in Germany, in agreement with a German scientific supervisor. Doctoral candidates can be funded for 2 to 12 months and postdocs for 2 to 6 months; the funding cannot be extended and cannot be split within the funding period. Value is a monthly scholarship payment of EUR 1,400 plus payments towards health, accident and personal liability insurance, a travel allowance, and for stays over six months a research allowance of EUR 460, a monthly rent subsidy and a monthly allowance for accompanying family members. German language support and TestDaF or DSH fee reimbursement are also limited to stays over six months. Eligibility requires that the doctorate started no more than 3 years before the deadline (or that a postdoc doctorate was completed no more than 4 years before it), that the doctorate is being done outside Germany, and that the applicant has not been resident in Germany for more than 15 months at the deadline. An independent selection committee of specialist scientists assesses academic qualification, the quality of the research project and the applicant's potential, also giving due consideration to equal opportunities. Applications are submitted online through the DAAD Portal, with deadlines updated annually in the second quarter.

new_scholarship.description: The DAAD University Summer Courses programme funds four-week German language, cultural studies and technical language courses at German universities and affiliated language schools for students and graduates from eligible countries. programme_detail_official.description: The aim of the DAAD University Summer Courses programme is to deepen knowledge of the German language, both general and technical, and to augment knowledge of regional studies. It funds students and graduates from eligible countries to attend four-week language, cultural studies and technical language courses at state or state-recognised German universities and affiliated language schools, taught exclusively in German and attended in person between June and September. The scholarship covers the cost of the language course, provides single-room accommodation through the course provider for the duration of the course, pays a one-time allowance of EUR 475, a country-specific travel allowance, and health, accident and personal liability insurance. Applicants must be enrolled at a university in a programme country other than Germany both at application and throughout the scholarship, be at least 18 at the start of the course, and prove German proficiency with a certificate no older than one year. Applications run from 1 September to 30 October each year, closing at 23:59 CET, and a selection committee reviews previous academic achievements and the letter of motivation.

programme_detail_official.description: The DAAD Helmut-Schmidt-Programme, also known as Public Policy and Good Governance, is designed to academically qualify future leaders in social and political science, law, economics, public policy and administration according to the principles of Good Governance. Funded by the Federal Foreign Office, it gives very well qualified graduates with a first university degree from developing or emerging countries the chance to obtain a master's degree in disciplines of special relevance for the social, political and economic development of their home country or region, and prepares them for future leadership positions in the Global South. Scholarships are granted for selected English-taught master's courses at seven participating German higher education institutions: Social Protection at Hochschule Bonn-Rhein-Sieg; Development and Governance at the University of Duisburg-Essen; Public Policy at the Erfurt School of Public Policy; Peace and Conflict Studies at the University of Magdeburg; Management in Nonprofit Organisations at Osnabrueck University of Applied Sciences; Development Studies and Governance and Public Policy at the University of Passau. Both young graduates and mid-career professionals may apply. Applications are submitted directly to the universities, not to the DAAD, during the 1 June to 31 July window. Scholarship holders study in small groups with special tutoring, take part in networking events and tailor-made workshops, and attend a German language course in Germany for up to six months before the master's studies.

new_scholarship.description: The DAAD Study Scholarship for Postgraduate Studies in the Field of Architecture funds a master's or postgraduate degree, or a complementary course not leading to a final qualification, at a state or state-recognised German university. Its objective on the awarding body's own announcement is to 'continue your education in Germany with a postgraduate or continuing course of study in the field of architecture'. Eligible first degrees are in architecture, interior design, monument conservation and building in existing contexts, urban design/development, landscape architecture and landscape planning. A fellowship runs between 10 and 24 months for a master's degree programme, or one academic year for complementary studies, with the start usually from 1 October of the year after application. The monthly payment is 992 euros, with a travel allowance on application, a one-off study allowance, and payments towards health, accident and personal liability insurance. The DAAD states that it does not cover tuition fees.
